summary.text: ODNI has publicly described accelerating AI adoption and strengthening cybersecurity in support of a presidential cyber strategy and AI framework. In August 2026, ODNI said a discussion covered priorities including accelerating AI under NSPM-11, implementing Zero Trust across IC networks, and an IARPA marketplace for non-traditional innovators. ODNI's January 2025 AI directive addresses coordination on privacy and civil liberties protections, guidance for AI trained on certain data, and periodic oversight reporting. An ODNI AI strategy document describes policy and legal efforts to reduce information-sharing barriers and an industry partnership plan covering data access, workforce skills, and advocacy for basic research funding.

Policies to codify AIM activities (e.g., acquisition, enterprise management, classification, and analytic integrity) will be developed with consultation from appropriate general counsel, civil liberties, privacy, and policy personnel. ODNI will provide a dedicated, integrated policy and legal effort to break down barriers to information sharing, particularly INT -specific data, so that we do not inadvertently slow the pace of technological progress.
